name: scalar-writers
what: time of one call of the escape of one context (xml, json, js, css, troff) for one value, in a loop over a list of 64 values that moves the output position by the count, as a render does; ns per value
purpose_in_the_task_list: Owner, 2026-11-14: a table of a scalar writer costs only what is needed; the media type as a compile-time parameter and a table built at run time in the Template are refused. Hypothesis: a table of classes of one byte in place of a table of words of 8 bytes keeps the speed of the word tables (arm 2, the form in include/ at f331cd1). This run answers whether it does
method: not the method of mbedded-cbor/bench/README.md: one run, 6 rounds, the arm order alternates by round (forward, then reversed), each process 5 repetitions of 2^22 input bytes for each input, timed with std::chrono::steady_clock; arm 6 is arm 2 built twice; arm 1 is not in this run; sysbench cpu 10 times for 1 s before the first round; each arm is held to the bytes of arm 0 before it is timed (every byte value alone and beside a letter, 16 pieces of js and troff at every position of every length 0 to 20, and every value of the inputs), with a room of escaped_size_max_in(context, n) + 32 bytes and guard bytes behind it; no gate, no steal

arms.0: the writers of include/mustache/escape.hpp at 4dac08e: a branch for each escaped byte, std::ranges::copy of each escape, a store of one byte for each plain byte
arms.2: each piece of output, a plain byte too, is one 8-byte word stored through std::span<char, 8>, std::bit_cast and std::copy_n, and the count moves on by the length of the piece; the word of each byte comes from a table of 256 words for each context, built at compile time; js tests the first byte of U+2028 and U+2029 and then starts_with; troff writes the first and the last place of a line apart from the table
arms.4: arm 2 with a class in place of a word: for each context a table of 256 classes of one byte (0 the byte stays; 1 a hex form made from the byte, in json, js and css; the next numbers a fixed replacement) and a table of the words of the classes (xml 6, json 9, js 2, css 2, troff 7 words of 8 bytes); the word of a byte is the word of its class OR the byte under a mask that is all ones where the class is 0, OR the two hex digits (made by arithmetic: nibble + '0', + 39 where the nibble is 10 or more) under a mask that is all ones where the class is 1; the classes are made at compile time from the word functions of arm 2; the writer stores one word and moves on by its length, js and troff keep their rules
arms.5: arm 4 with the classes of the five contexts in bit fields of one table of 256 entries of 16 bits (xml bits 0 to 2, json 3 to 6, js 7, css 8, troff 9 to 11); the class is the entry shifted right and masked
arms.6: the same code as arm 2, a second binary: the noise of the cell

inputs.<n>-<p>: 64 values of n bytes (16, 64, 1024) from letters, digits and a space; each byte is a mark of the context with the probability p percent (0 or 5); marks: xml &<>"', json " \ line feed and 0x01, js ' < \ /, css ' } < \, troff \ " ' ` ~ ^; fixed seed
inputs.lines-<n>-<p>: troff only: the same with a line feed at every 16th byte

builds: g++-16 and clang++-23, -O2 and -Os, -march=x86-64-v3; -std=c++26 -DNDEBUG -Wall -Wextra -Werror -falign-functions=64 -falign-loops=64 (g++ also -falign-jumps=64) -DARM=<arm>; one binary for each arm and build
arms_in_this_run: 0 2 6 4 5 (order of the first round; the order reverses in each even round)

notes: Every process passed the check against arm 0 before its timing. No process failed.
The median of arm 4 is above the median of arm 2 in 129 of 136 cells, the median of arm 5 in 133 of 136 cells.

The generated code of arms 4 and 5 has no branch on the class in the builds that were read (g++-16 -O2 and -Os, clang++-23 -O2; a cmov for each mask) and makes three loads for each input byte (the byte, the class, the word of the class); arm 2 makes two.
With g++-16 -Os, hex_pair_of (not marked always_inline) is called once for each input byte in the json, js and css loops of arms 4 and 5; with -O2 and with clang++-23 it is inlined.
Arm 6 is the code of arm 2. On g++-16 -O2 its median is 0.63 to 1.06 of arm 2, so the cells of arm 2 on that build have a noise of up to 37 percent in this run.
